claims.text: The starting eutectic high-entropy alloy has a hierarchical microstructure of dual-phase lamellar colonies.
The untreated alloy has limited room-temperature tensile ductility and exhibits brittle or premature catastrophic failure.
Dislocation pile-ups at internal lamellar boundaries produce local stress concentrations, microcracking, and premature failure in the untreated alloy.
The proposed intervention is repeated thermal cycling at 500°C for 5 minutes per cycle followed by rapid air cooling.
Cyclic thermal annealing activates recovery processes in the alloy.
Thermally activated recovery allows dislocations to rearrange and annihilate at lamellar boundaries.
Cyclic thermal annealing promotes localized nanoscale phase precipitation at lamellar interfaces.
The proposed interfacial nanophase acts as a dislocation sink and absorbs dislocations.
The proposed nanoscale interfacial phase provides precipitation strengthening.
Dislocation rearrangement, annihilation, and interfacial precipitation reduce dislocation pile-ups and local stress concentrations.
Reducing interfacial pile-ups and stress concentrations delays microcrack initiation.
Relative to the untreated alloy, cyclically annealed material will have greater room-temperature tensile ductility and extended plastic deformation.
Relative to the untreated alloy, cyclically annealed material will retain or slightly increase tensile strength.
The effectiveness of the treatment may depend on the precise thermal-cycle parameters and resulting microstructural evolution.
